subject: zoology
question_text: Mention any two substances secreted by mast cells and their functions.

verification.note: Sourced from the Sri Chaitanya Junior Fastrack zoology section (book p.51, VSAQ 79). Zoology holds only ONE source book — the TSBIE Basic Learning Material in hand covers physics only, and no zoology board paper is in the corpus — so the two-book union check and the back-test are both structurally impossible for this card; 'not checked' does NOT mean 'checked and clean'. The mark split is a claim until a Telangana IPE teacher confirms it.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: What mast cells secrete
steps.why: The question asks for any two, so naming the short full list first makes sure two correct names are already on the page.
common_mistakes: Naming only one substance. The question asks for two.
Confusing mast cells with plasma cells. Plasma cells make antibodies.
steps.memory_tip: Four names in one list: heparin, histamine, bradykinin, serotonin.
steps.margin_note: Name the cell and then the substances. Two lines.
lines: Mast cells are cells of connective tissue.

steps.label: What each one does
steps.why: Each mark here is a substance PAIRED with its function, so a name written without its job earns nothing.
common_mistakes: Writing the names without their functions. The function is half of each mark.
Calling serotonin a vasodilator. It narrows the vessels.
steps.memory_tip: Histamine and bradykinin widen; serotonin narrows; heparin keeps the blood liquid.
steps.margin_note: Two substances with their functions is the full answer. Boxing the pair makes it easy to read.
lines: Heparin is an anticoagulant: it stops the blood
Serotonin is a vasoconstrictor: it narrows

insider_note: The mark is the PAIR — substance plus function — so never write a bare list of four names and stop there.
